_readme: Pinned llama.cpp release. The port NEVER compiles llama.cpp (docs/PORTING_NOTES.md
§ Linux/IoT: DO NOT COMPILE llama.cpp); it runs an official prebuilt llama-server.
NEVER TRUST THE NETWORK ALONE. Every asset listed here is downloaded and then
verified against the sha256 recorded below before anything is extracted or
executed. A variant with an empty sha256 is treated as UNPINNED and is refused
rather than downloaded: an unverified 170 MB binary that the service then execs is
exactly the thing this file exists to prevent.
GOTCHA, cost us a wrong pin once: DO NOT USE /releases/latest. The GitHub API
returns the stray tag v0.4.1 for this repo (verified again 2026-09-15: the latest
endpoint answered v0.4.1 published 2026-09-14T18:27:29Z while the newest real
build was b10976). The v0.4.1 tag exists because the shared libraries carry that
soname - the tarballs ship libllama-common.so.0.4.1 - not because it is a release
anyone should run. Query the releases LIST and match tags against ^b[0-9]+$.
How these digests were produced (2026-09-15): the releases list was queried, the
b10970 tag read, and each asset's sha256 taken from the GitHub asset `digest`
field. That field was independently checked by downloading
llama-b10970-bin-ubuntu-arm64.tar.gz in full and hashing it locally; the two
agreed. Re-verify the same way when bumping the tag (`make pin-runtime`).
Tarball layout, verified on the arm64 asset: a single top-level directory named
after the tag (llama-b10970/) holding llama-server alongside the shared libraries
it needs (libllama.so.0, libmtmd.so.0, libggml*.so). The extractor keeps that tree
intact and the supervisor sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH to the directory the binary lives
in, because these builds do not carry an rpath.
